records.Entity / project type: integrated Lightning payment company / merchant platform
records.Concise description: Lightning-powered payment company whose integrated ecosystem spans merchant acceptance infrastructure, payment APIs and a custodial consumer/business wallet.
records.Deeper researched summary: Speed began with a merchant-focused Lightning API and now describes Speed Merchant as an enterprise payment layer for accepting Bitcoin and stablecoins, alongside Speed Wallet and broader payout infrastructure. The company therefore receives one PAYMENTS profile rather than separate Merchant, API and wallet records. Its current wallet documentation describes the wallet as custodial; the exact custody and settlement architecture for every enterprise merchant deployment is not fully documented publicly and should not be inferred from the wallet alone.
records.Launch / history: Founded in 2021; an official December 2025 company history describes an evolution from merchant-focused Lightning API to Speed Merchant, Speed Wallet and broader payment infrastructure.
records.Why it matters in the Bitcoin payments e: It captures a newer generation of Lightning-native payment companies integrating merchant acceptance, APIs and hosted end-user balances into one system.
Important technical or cultural characte: One integrated company profile to prevent product duplication

Official sources.label: Speed company history / December 2025 funding announcement

records.Verification basis: Current official site plus the company's December 2025 product history verify active Speed Merchant and the merchant-API lineage through the current period.
Research notes / uncertainties: Do not transfer the custodial label from Speed Wallet to every enterprise merchant integration without product-specific evidence.
Do not use company-reported volume/user metrics as timeless inclusion claims.
Because Speed also has a wallet, Master Explore should preserve one canonical entity and relate WALLETS rather than create a duplicate product profile.

records.Entity / project type: legacy self-custodial crypto merchant checkout product
records.Concise description: Coinbase's former merchant checkout product, included for its Bitcoin-era payment history but classified inactive after Coinbase required migration away from Commerce by March 31, 2026.
records.Deeper researched summary: Coinbase Commerce historically let merchants create crypto charges using self-custodial Commerce wallets. Coinbase's current transition notice states the Commerce portal became permanently inaccessible after March 31, 2026 and merchants can no longer create Commerce charges or use its dashboard. The replacement Coinbase Business is described as stablecoin-first and custodial, so it should not silently inherit Commerce's historical Bitcoin profile. A legacy Coinbase status page still displaying Commerce components as operational conflicts with the transition notice and is treated as stale/ambiguous operational telemetry rather than evidence of an active merchant product.
records.Launch / history: Launched in 2018 as Coinbase's merchant crypto checkout product; retired into a Coinbase Business transition with a March 31, 2026 deadline.
records.Why it matters in the Bitcoin payments e: It was a major branded merchant checkout product and its 2026 retirement illustrates a shift from self-custodial multi-asset merchant checkout toward custodial/stablecoin business infrastructure.
Important technical or cultural characte: Bitcoin was historically supported, though late Commerce network support narrowed
Replacement Coinbase Business has different custody and asset positioning

Official sources.label: Coinbase Help — Transitioning from Coinbase Commerce to Coinbase Business

records.Verification basis: Coinbase's first-party transition notice is explicit that the Commerce portal and charge creation end after March 31, 2026; this outweighs the legacy status page's apparently operational component labels for lifecycle classification.
Research notes / uncertainties: Publication copy must explain the conflict between the explicit retirement notice and the still-reachable status telemetry.
Do not describe Coinbase Business as the same Bitcoin payment product; its replacement architecture and asset scope differ materially.
Do not publish old Bitcoin-network support lists as current Commerce functionality.

records.Entity / project type: hosted multi-asset payment processor with material Bitcoin usage
records.Concise description: Hosted crypto payment processor whose current checkout still materially supports Bitcoin on-chain and Lightning, with merchant conversion and settlement options.
records.Deeper researched summary: CoinGate is broader than Bitcoin, but Bitcoin remains important enough to warrant PAYMENTS inclusion: its current merchant checkout supports BTC and Lightning, while an official H1 2026 report continued to show Bitcoin as a major payment asset/network. Standard merchant flows use a CoinGate account for processing, conversion and settlement rather than direct payment to an arbitrary merchant self-custody address. KYC/KYB, fiat settlement and jurisdiction support are part of the hosted-service model.
records.Launch / history: Operating since the 2010s as a cryptocurrency payment gateway and expanding from Bitcoin-centered acceptance into a broader multi-asset processor.
records.Why it matters in the Bitcoin payments e: It is a useful boundary case: a company need not be Bitcoin-only to be canonical when current Bitcoin and Lightning payment significance remains demonstrably material.
records.Verification basis: Current official checkout material verifies BTC/Lightning support; CoinGate's dated H1 2026 company reporting confirms Bitcoin remains materially used rather than a token legacy feature.
Research notes / uncertainties: Do not repeat H1 2026 payment-share metrics without a date.
Fees, supported assets, settlement currencies and jurisdictions are time-sensitive.
CoinGate is included despite multi-asset scope because Bitcoin significance is current and material, not because every crypto processor belongs in PAYMENTS.

records.Concise description: NFC tap-to-pay ecosystem for Lightning payments, spanning CoinCorner's custodial card product and open-source/self-hosted Bolt Card-compatible implementations.
records.Deeper researched summary: The Bolt Card uses NFC with LNURL-based payment flows so a user can tap compatible merchant hardware rather than scan a Lightning invoice QR code. CoinCorner operates a commercial Bolt Card linked to a CoinCorner balance, while open-source Bolt Card/LNbits-oriented deployments can use different backends. Custody therefore cannot be stated once for the whole ecosystem: CoinCorner's product is account/custodial, whereas DIY or self-hosted deployments inherit the trust model of their LNbits/funding source.
Creators / founders: CoinCorner team and open-source Bolt Card contributors
records.Launch / history: Developed in the early 2020s as a Lightning NFC payment concept; commercial and interoperable/open-source implementations followed.
records.Why it matters in the Bitcoin payments e: It is a meaningful physical payment UX layer that demonstrates Lightning acceptance without a phone-screen QR scan and exposes how payment UX can be separated from the wallet/custody backend.
records.Verification basis: Current CoinCorner support plus the open-source Bolt Card project verify active NFC/Lightning use and the distinct commercial versus DIY deployment models.
Research notes / uncertainties: As of 2026-08-15, CoinCorner documents current UK setup/linking restrictions tied to regulatory changes; do not generalize that constraint to all Bolt Card implementations.
Do not call Bolt Card itself a wallet or assign one universal custody model.
